BLOCKED: nothing was committed or pushed. The slice stopped on a defect in how the compiler lowers a callback passed into a host trait; the report is at /home/user/Nikaia/docs/briefs/k3a2-comptime-compute.md.report.md.

**The defect:** the checker accepts using a `fn` parameter twice when it goes to a trait method with no body. The trait method counts as keeping the callback, so it lowers as `nikaia_std::func::Kept`. The generated Rust then moves that value on the first call and never clones it, although `Kept` can be cloned. So rustc refuses it with "use of moved value". Minimal probe:

```
trait H { fn ask(ref self, known: fn(ref String) -> i64? sync) -> i64? sync }
fn twice[T: H](host: ref T, known: fn(ref String) -> i64? sync) -> i64 {
    let a = host.ask(known) ?? 0
    let b = host.ask(known) ?? 0
    return a + b
}
fn main() { println("x") }
```

`nikaia run` on it gives "Use of moved value: `known`". `comptime_computed` passes `known` and `typed` to the host many times (once inside a loop) and then to itself, so the move cannot be built until this is fixed. `ref fn(..)` does not parse as a parameter type, so the trait cannot borrow the callback instead.

**What I built before stopping:** step 2 in `comptime_tree.nika`: the `ComptimeComputeHost` trait, `comptime_computed`, `comptime_worked_out_ahead` and the four consts. `lower-std` accepts it; only the Rust it generates fails, as above. I saved it at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Nikaia/8a3a29dc-69fc-49cd-abeb-78092aa24a1f/scratchpad/k3a2/k3a2-nika.patch and restored my three files by name. The report lists what the next run needs to write differently.

**Also met:** a trait method with a `fn` parameter cannot be implemented in Nikaia: it is refused with "has 1 type parameter but its trait declaration has 0". The host here is Rust, so this one did not block the move.
